title: Employer Benefit Charging Bulletin: Monthly Protest Interest
content:
**Subject:** monthly protest interest on a written protest of Employer Benefit Charging charges that disputes the employer's base-period wages or its base-period status.

**Rule.** The monthly protest interest is, when the employer's tax account shows interest assessed for the statement's quarter and an amount billed for that quarter, the latest month of that assessed interest in proportion to the protested principal over the amount billed for the quarter; when no interest has yet been assessed for that quarter but the employer finances benefits by reimbursement and the bill for the quarter is past its due date, the protested principal times the late-payment interest rate of the employer's tax account class; and nothing otherwise.

**Records.** Every input is read from the employer's Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts record for the statement's quarter:

- *interest assessed* — the interest entries assessed on that quarter; the latest month of assessed interest is the amount of the most recently assessed entry;
- *amount billed for the quarter* — the total of the reimbursement bills entered for that quarter;
- *financing* — the tax account's financing class (a "Reimbursing —" class finances by reimbursement);
- *the late-payment interest rate* — the monthly late-payment interest rate that the employer's tax account class carries in Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts.

**Branches.**

| Interest assessed for the quarter | Amount billed for the quarter | Reimbursing, with the bill past its due date | Monthly protest interest |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Either | The latest month of assessed interest, multiplied by the protested principal and divided by the amount billed for the quarter |
| No | Yes | Yes | The protested principal multiplied by the class's monthly late-payment interest rate |
| Yes | No | — | Nothing |
| No | Either | No | Nothing |

Interest assessed on a quarter for which nothing has been billed meets neither of the first two branches, so no monthly protest interest arises. The monthly protest interest is carried unrounded; rounding to the cent happens only once it has been multiplied by the number of interest months.

**Worked figures (hypothetical).**

- Latest month of assessed interest $18.00; amount billed for the quarter $2,400.00; protested principal $1,200.00. The monthly protest interest is 18.00 multiplied by 1,200.00 and divided by 2,400.00: $9.00.
- No interest yet assessed; a reimbursing employer's bill is past due; protested principal $1,200.00; a class rate taken for illustration as one per cent a month. The monthly protest interest is 1,200.00 multiplied by that rate: $12.00.
- Interest of $18.00 assessed on a contributory employer's quarter with no reimbursement bill for it: nothing.
